subtype: Exams, tuition, family and friends together [Actor]
passage: Class teacher's note, third week of November. I'm Sangeeta, and I've noticed Hansa changing. The maths coaching is at 5, the school unit test is Monday, an uncle's family visits on Sunday, and Hansa also promised to help a friend with a class poster. Hansa did not say the load was too much. Instead, Hansa snapped at the desk partner over a borrowed pencil and rolled eyes when I asked about homework. This morning Hansa's eyes were red, and a small comment about the fan led to a sharp word. I did not scold. I asked Hansa to stay after the bell, gave a glass of water and said, “You seem stretched. What could we move?”

qa.a: The school unit test is on Monday.

qa.q: What might Hansa be feeling behind the snapping at the desk partner?
qa.a: Hansa is likely overwhelmed and stretched thin; the irritability shows the overload before any clear complaint does.

qa.q: What did Sangeeta do instead of scolding?
qa.a: Sangeeta asked Hansa to stay after the bell, gave a glass of water and asked what could be moved.

qa.q: How might the desk partner have felt about the snapped word over the pencil?
qa.a: The desk partner was probably surprised and hurt by a sharp reaction to a small thing, and may not know the real cause was overload.

grounding: A teenager juggling school, coaching, family and friends shows the overload first as irritability.

subtype: Exams, tuition, family and friends together [Actor]
passage: Sunday night. I'm too tired to think properly, so this will be short. Tuition at 4, unit test tomorrow, Mausi's family here for lunch, and Payal and I said we'd go to the shop for chart paper. I was okay until dinner. Then Payal asked if I could pass the salt and I said “Can't you see I'm busy?” loudly enough that everyone looked up. Payal's face went small. Ma didn't say anything, just kept eating. I feel awful. The strange thing is I wasn't angry at Payal at all. I think I'm just full, like a glass that's been overflowing all day. I'll say sorry in the morning. — Himani

qa.q: What did Himani say when Payal asked for the salt?
qa.a: Himani said, “Can't you see I'm busy?” loudly enough that everyone looked up.

qa.q: What does Himani mean by “a glass that's been overflowing”?
qa.a: Himani feels overloaded and worn out, so the anger came out at the nearest person even though Himani was not really angry at Payal.

qa.q: What could Himani do tomorrow to help with the overload?
qa.a: Say sorry to Payal, and tell Ma that the week is too full so that something, like the shop trip, can be moved.

qa.q: How might Payal have felt when Himani snapped?
qa.a: Payal's face went small, which suggests hurt and confusion at being snapped at over a simple request.

grounding: A teenager juggling exams, tuition, family and friends shows overload as irritability toward those nearby.
